study_type_evidence.quote: Lean mice were administered sc (5 mL/kg, 10 nmol/mL) and blood sampled at eight time-points within 24 h.
NMRI mice (n = 32), acclimatized for 5 days, were randomized into four groups (n = 8 per group) based on body weight
A stable HEK293 cell line expressing the Epac cAMP-sensor as well as the GLP-1 receptor was used for functional screening

in_vitro_detail: HEK293 cells stably expressing the human GLP-1 receptor and an Epac FRET cAMP biosensor were used for GLP-1R potency (EC50) screening. Biophysical work was cell-free: size exclusion chromatography and dynamic light scattering in PBS pH 7.4, and surface plasmon resonance (Biacore X100) against 3555 RU of immobilized human serum albumin on a CM5 chip.

notes: PDF-derived text with ABSTRACT NOT FENCED: the abstract is the paragraph beginning 'ABSTRACT: Noncovalent binding of biopharmaceuticals to human serum albumin' and ending '...compared to its monovalent equivalent', immediately before the INTRODUCTION heading. It was identified and excluded; every value above comes from RESULTS, DISCUSSION, figure captions or the EXPERIMENTAL SECTION. PK was measured only for analogues 4 and 6, in C57Bl/6 mice; all other in vivo work (OGTT, food intake) used NMRI mice. Doses are given only as a volume/concentration pair (5 mL/kg of a 10 nmol/mL solution); the body never states a nmol/kg dose, so no conversion was performed. Two internal inconsistencies are recorded rather than resolved: (i) the Results state analogue 6 had 'a circulatory half-life of 299 m' whereas the Discussion says '299 min'; (ii) the Methods list the OGTT arms as vehicle, peptide 2, 4 or 6 while the Results and Figure 3 caption list vehicle, liraglutide, 4 or 6, and Figure 3 states n = 7 per group while the Methods state n = 8 per group. No absorption half-life is reported anywhere in the body: protracted absorption for analogue 6 is evidenced only by the later tmax (~4 h vs 0.5 h), which is recorded under tmax and not under any half-life field. No sequence is printed in the body; the backbone is described only as [K34R]-GLP-1(7-37)-OH, so all sequences are 'not reported' (the PepLife2 header sequence was not used). Linagliptin was added to blood collection tubes as a DPP-IV inhibitor rather than administered to animals, so it is not listed as an agent.
